## Correctness / openprot-no-panic

1. `resolve_cs` in target/ast10x0/peripherals/smc/controller.rs (~line 403) only rejects a geometry whose `capacity_bytes` overflows the CS's aperture share; it never rejects `capacity_bytes == 0` or a non-power-of-two `page_size`/`sector_size`/`block_size`. For the `Discover` (SFDP) path the decoder happens to guarantee sector/block are powers of two, but `capacity_bytes` can legitimately decode to 0 from a corrupt/misparsed BFP table (density < 8 bits, see `BasicFlashParams::density_bits`), and for the `Pinned` marker path there is *no* validation at all -- a target that hardcodes a typo'd `FlashGeometry` (e.g. `page_size: 0`) sails straight through `Smc::init`. That degenerate geometry then reaches `hal/blocking/flash/flash.rs`'s `BlockingFlash::program`, which does `assert!(program_window_size.count_ones() == 1, ...)` on exactly this value -- i.e. a bad SFDP decode or a bad `Pinned` constant becomes a runtime panic instead of a typed error surfaced to the caller. This is a real regression risk introduced by moving from statically-known-good `FlashConfig` constants to dynamically-resolved geometry, and matches the "SFDP misparse leaves the driver in an inconsistent state" failure mode this stack needs to guard against. Fix: validate capacity/page/sector/block once in `resolve_cs` (see suggested diff) so both geometry sources are equally guarded, instead of relying on each downstream consumer to re-check.
2. target/ast10x0/backend/flash/src/lib.rs `Ast10x0FmcFlashDriver::size()` does `NonZero::new(self.geometry.capacity_bytes as usize).expect("capacity validated in new()")`. `.expect()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` is flagged regardless of how confident the comment is that it can't fail; since `new()` already proves the value non-zero, store the `NonZero<usize>` once as a field and return it directly, removing the panic path entirely (see suggested diff).

## Verbosity / over-engineering (ponytail-review)

3. This PR introduces the codebase's only two `#![feature(...)]` gates (`associated_type_defaults`, `adt_const_params`, in target/ast10x0/peripherals/lib.rs and util/sfdp/lib.rs) purely so `SmcInstance::Cs0Geometry`/`Cs1Geometry` can pick between `Discover` and `Pinned<const G: FlashGeometry>` at the type level, letting an unused SFDP-decode path be dead-code-eliminated. The repo already pins a nightly toolchain, but nothing else in the tree relies on unstable features, and the SFDP decoder is a few hundred bytes of pure byte parsing -- the "must not link the decoder" motivation is a small win for taking on two unstable, still-evolving language features (`adt_const_params` in particular has changed shape upstream more than once). A plain runtime-selected value (e.g. `enum GeometrySource { Discover, Pinned(FlashGeometry) }` as an associated `const` on `SmcInstance`) would express the same policy on stable Rust for a few extra bytes of flash, and would not be exposed to the next nightly bump breaking this one PR's code. Worth simplifying unless the link-time savings were actually measured and matter.

## Nits

4. target/ast10x0/peripherals/smc/controller.rs, `Pinned`'s doc comment: "for production buils when the wired flash is sure not to change Its `resolve`..." -- typo ("buils" -> "builds") and a missing sentence break before "Its" (should be lowercase, mid-sentence).
5. Several QEMU test targets (e.g. target/ast10x0/tests/smc/dma_irq/target.rs, tests/smc/read/target.rs) use `unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(...) }` on hardcoded DMA addresses without a `// SAFETY:` comment. Pre-existing pattern in this test code (not newly introduced by this PR), but worth cleaning up opportunistically since the PR is already touching every one of these files.
